title: Maheshwar
source_note: NCERT structural alignment only. Zidd uses original teaching passages, checks, and feedback instead of copying the textbook body.

levels.title: Read facts in a dialogue
levels.teaching_goal: Use speaker clues in a dialogue to find important facts about a historical place.

guided_check.teaching_block: In a dialogue, facts can come through what one speaker explains to another. Track the speaker, then the fact.
guided_check.passage: Chachi told the children that the old fort was linked with Queen Ahilya Bai and her care for the town.
guided_check.prompt: Who is linked with the fort in this dialogue?

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: location details often name a river, town, hill, or state.
bridge.passage: The guide said the fort stood high above the town, with a wide river flowing nearby.
bridge.prompt: Which detail tells us about the fort's location?

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: separate people facts from place facts. A queen is a person; a river or town tells location.
masterclass.passage: The teacher said the palace stood beside the Narmada River and was watched over by a statue.
masterclass.prompt: Which phrase names the river near the place?

independent_check.teaching_block: Now find the location fact without hints.
independent_check.passage: The family visited a fort on a hill near the Narmada River and looked down at the town.
independent_check.prompt: Which river is near the fort?

levels.title: Identify fort features
levels.teaching_goal: Read descriptive clues about a historical monument and its special features.

guided_check.teaching_block: A feature is a special part of a place. In monument descriptions, look for words that name what visitors can see.
guided_check.passage: The old fort had stone steps, carved doors, and overhanging balconies that looked out over the river.
guided_check.prompt: Which feature looked out over the river?

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: materials tell what something is made from.
bridge.passage: The palace wall was built with red stones brought from faraway quarries.
bridge.prompt: What material was used for the wall?

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: do not mix a feature with a feeling. Grand staircases are a feature; excited is a feeling.
masterclass.passage: Visitors admired the grand staircases and the shaded balconies of the fort.
masterclass.prompt: Which phrase names a feature of the fort?

independent_check.teaching_block: Now identify the building material without hints.
independent_check.passage: The guide explained that the fort walls were made from red stones carried from another region.
independent_check.prompt: What were the fort walls made from?

levels.title: Find the odd word out
levels.teaching_goal: Group words with similar meanings and identify the word that does not fit.

guided_check.teaching_block: Synonyms have similar meanings. If three words mean sad, the happy word is the odd one out.
guided_check.prompt: Which word does not belong with the sad words?

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: talk, discuss, and speak are communication words.
bridge.prompt: Which word does not name a way of communicating?

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: first name the group idea. Noisy is different from quiet, silent, and calm.
masterclass.prompt: Which word is the odd one out?

independent_check.teaching_block: Now find the odd word without hints.
independent_check.prompt: Which word does not fit the group?

levels.title: Spot silent g words
levels.teaching_goal: Recognize words where the letter g is written but not clearly pronounced.

guided_check.teaching_block: Some English words keep a written letter that we do not say strongly. In sign, the g is silent.
guided_check.passage: The guide pointed to the sign near the palace gate.
guided_check.prompt: Which word has a silent g?

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: design also has a silent g sound.
bridge.passage: The cloth design used bright lines and small checks.
bridge.prompt: Which word has a silent g?

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: read the whole word aloud. If you do not hear the g clearly, mark it as silent.
masterclass.passage: The artist made a sign with a flower design.
masterclass.prompt: Which pair has silent g words?

independent_check.teaching_block: Now choose the silent-g word without hints.
independent_check.passage: The saree design had a red border.
independent_check.prompt: Which word has a silent g?

levels.title: Choose a, an, or the
levels.teaching_goal: Use a, an, and the before nouns with the right meaning.

guided_check.teaching_block: Use an before a word that begins with a vowel sound, like apple or old.
guided_check.passage: The child saw ___ old gate near the fort.

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: use the when you mean a specific thing already known.
bridge.passage: A guide showed us a statue. Later, ___ statue looked golden in the sunlight.
bridge.prompt: Which article points to the same statue again?

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: choose a for one new consonant-sound noun, an for one new vowel-sound noun, and the for a specific noun.
masterclass.passage: We carried ___ umbrella because rain clouds covered the sky.

independent_check.teaching_block: Now choose the specific article without hints.
independent_check.passage: A child found a key near the gate. ___ key opened the old room.
independent_check.prompt: Which article shows we mean the same key?
